symptom: On a run where lint BUILDS the catalog, one iterator failed while others succeeded on the same handle: `lint could not read the catalog for AttributesFor: SQL logic error: no such table: attributes` with ctx.Entities() returning rows in the same run, and the next identical run (cached catalog) correct. Reproduced on testdata/testapp-views and not on testdata/pedapp. Also: a fresh catalog's snapshot ObjectCount was counted as 0.
cause: catalog.New() opened `sql.Open("sqlite", ":memory:")`. Every CONNECTION to ":memory:" is its own separate, empty database, and sql.Open returns a POOL — so createTables' schema landed on one connection and whatever query the pool later served on another saw nothing. Which iterator broke was pool timing, hence the per-project difference. Fixed with a uniquely named shared-cache DSN (`file:mxcli-catalog-<pid>-<n>?mode=memory&cache=shared&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)`) plus one pinned connection so the shared cache is not freed. Two rejected fixes mattered: db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) gives one database but DEADLOCKS, because the readers nest (ctx.Entities() yields from an open cursor while the body calls ctx.AttributesFor()) and because Builder.updateSnapshotCount queried the POOL while the build transaction held a connection; shared cache alone still hung on that same builder read until it was routed through b.txQuery.
insight: ":memory:" plus database/sql is never one database — it is one per connection, so any pooled access is a coin flip, and the failure presents as a MISSING TABLE on a schema that provably exists (sqlite_master listed all 88 views in the failing run). That signature — one table unreadable while its neighbours read fine, same handle, same run — means separate databases, not a broken view; stop comparing view DDL and look at the DSN. The per-project reproduction (one project yes, one no) is the tell that it is pool timing rather than data. Pinning the pool is the obvious fix and is wrong here: a goroutine dump taken with kill -QUIT named the exact blocker (Builder.updateSnapshotCount -> QueryRow -> database/sql.(*DB).conn), and it only showed up because the hang was investigated instead of the pin reverted. Reading a count on the pool while the build transaction is open was also returning 0, because a pool query cannot see the transaction's uncommitted rows: the deadlock and the wrong count were one bug. Finally, a claim about CI behaviour needs the exit code, not the printed text: lint already prints "Results are INCOMPLETE" and exits 1 on any recorded query error (cmd_lint.go), so the "CI sees a pass" worry in the issue was unfounded.
